# Review Checklist: Free-Text Grading via a Real A2A Service

**Purpose**: Standard PR-review-level requirements-quality pass across the full spec -- security guardrails, the A2A/independent-deployability claims, and grading-correctness/mastery-integration requirements, per reviewer request.
**Created**: 2026-08-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for how a legitimately flawed rubric on an individual free-text question (as opposed to systemically flawed Grading Agent scoring logic) gets corrected? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] -- Fixed 2026-08-19: FR-002 now states an individually flawed rubric is corrected via Milestone 1's existing FR-011 flagging mechanism, not a new path.
- [x] CHK002 Are minimum/maximum bounds on the number of rubric criteria per free-text question specified? [Gap, Spec §Key Entities: Grading Rubric] -- Fixed: FR-002 now states >=1 criterion required, no fixed maximum, single-criterion (weight 1.0) explicitly valid.
- [x] CHK003 Is a learner-facing "grading in progress" state specified for the interval between submission and grading completion? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] -- Fixed: new Edge Cases bullet + FR-018 name this as a fifth distinct state.
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for a learner double-submitting the same free-text answer (e.g., a duplicate client-side click), as distinct from FR-010's server-side network-retry case? [Gap, Edge Case] -- Fixed: new Edge Cases bullet clarifies the existing per-question single-submission guard already covers this, no free-text-specific handling needed.
- [x] CHK005 Is behavior specified for an in-flight free-text submission when the learner navigates away or the session ends before grading completes? [Gap] -- Fixed: new Edge Cases bullet -- grading is a stateless server-side cycle independent of client presence.
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for whether a learner is notified when their account crosses FR-013's review-flag threshold, or only silently flagged? [Gap, Spec §FR-013] -- Fixed: FR-013 now explicitly states no learner notification occurs.
- [x] CHK007 Are requirements defined for the two seeded subjects' minimum free-text coverage (e.g., is "at least one topic per subject" itself a requirement, or only an Assumption)? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions vs FR-001] -- Fixed: promoted into FR-001 itself as a MUST, no longer only an Assumption.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Does the moderation-rejection message reuse the term "on-topic" consistently with its distinct meaning in the off-topic/nonsensical edge case, which explicitly is NOT grounds for rejection (rubric-graded normally instead)? [Consistency/Clarity, Spec §FR-012 vs §Edge Cases] -- Fixed 2026-08-19: message reworded to "content flagged -- please revise and resubmit your answer" throughout spec.md and contracts/api.md; "on-topic" no longer used for the moderation state.
- [x] CHK009 Is "toxic or abusive" (FR-012) given any scope, category, or example, or left entirely undefined pending implementation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012] -- Fixed: FR-012 now names the category (harassment, hate speech, sexually explicit material, threats of violence) while still deferring exact classification approach to plan time.
- [x] CHK010 Is "embedded instructions" (FR-014) scoped clearly enough to distinguish a genuine prompt-injection attempt from an answer that legitimately discusses instructions as its subject matter? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014] -- Fixed: FR-014 now states the distinction is behavioral (text addressed at the grader) not topical.
- [x] CHK011 Are the four rejection states (too-long, rate-limited, moderation-rejected, grading-unavailable) each specified with a distinct learner-facing message, or only distinguished by internal error codes? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases] -- Fixed: new FR-018 requires each of the five named states (including grading-in-progress) to have its own distinct message.
- [x] CHK012 Is "near-threshold-score" (used in the ground-truth set requirement, FR-008) quantified, or left to later interpretation of how near "near" is? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008] -- Fixed: FR-008 now defines "near" relative to FR-005's locked threshold, with the margin itself locked at plan time.
- [x] CHK013 Is "account-level review" (FR-013) defined precisely enough to distinguish it from Milestone 1's per-question flagging, given both currently have "no reviewer yet" as their only specified behavior? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013] -- Fixed: FR-013 now explicitly scopes the count to FR-012 moderation rejections only, distinguishing its granularity from M1's per-question flag.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK014 Are "Grading Rubric" (immutable, generated once per question) and "Grading Logic Version" (versioned, evolves independently) used consistently -- never conflated -- across Requirements, Key Entities, and Success Criteria? [Consistency] -- Reviewed, no defect found: grep confirms no stale "rubric version" phrasing remains outside the historical Clarifications log entry that originally raised the question.
- [x] CHK015 Do FR-005's graduated-score-then-threshold design and FR-006's "exact same mechanism...structured question's grading result" agree on what "same mechanism" means once free-text introduces a graduated score upstream of the binary mastery-update path? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005 vs FR-006] -- Fixed: FR-006 now explicitly scopes "same mechanism" to the mastery-update step from the binary signal onward.
- [x] CHK016 Are the four guardrail rejection reasons (too-long, rate-limited, moderation, injection-triggered-invalid-response) treated as mutually exclusive and consistently ordered wherever more than one could apply to the same submission? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012/FR-014/FR-015/FR-016] -- Fixed: new FR-017 establishes a fixed precedence order.
- [x] CHK017 Is the retry policy described identically everywhere it's referenced (FR-010, FR-014, SC-006), with no implied difference in retry count or backoff between the two FRs? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010 vs FR-014] -- Fixed: FR-010 now explicitly cross-references FR-014 as the same single policy.
- [x] CHK018 Is spec.md's framing of the double-counting risk consistent with what the quiz feature's prior bug actually was, or does it overstate the similarity in a way that could mislead an implementer's design choice? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases] -- Fixed 2026-08-19: edge case now states the two bugs share only the broad category (double-counting a single answer's effect), explicitly notes the quiz bug's specific mechanism (same-transaction re-read) differs from this feature's (retried network call), and its fix is not directly reusable -- matching research.md §4's own correction.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality (Measurability)

- [x] CHK019 Can SC-003's "agreed accuracy/consistency threshold" be objectively verified from the spec alone, or does it require a value fixed elsewhere that the spec doesn't cross-reference? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003] -- Fixed: SC-003 now explicitly names `research.md` as where the locked value is recorded, making it traceable.
- [x] CHK020 Is SC-005's "demonstrated at least once" specified precisely enough to be a pass/fail gate, or does it rely on a reviewer's subjective judgment of what counts as a valid demonstration? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005] -- Fixed: SC-005 now lists three required, objective conditions for the demonstration.
- [x] CHK021 Can SC-008's claim (an injected instruction "did not change the recorded grade") be objectively tested without the spec further specifying a corpus or class of injection-attempt examples to test against? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008] -- Fixed: FR-008 now requires the ground-truth set to include a prompt-injection-attempt triple, and SC-008 references that same corpus.
- [x] CHK022 Do FR-015/FR-016's length cap and rate limit have any spec-stated bound, range, or order-of-magnitude guidance, or are they fully open until `/speckit-plan` fixes a number? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015 vs FR-016] -- Fixed: both FRs now state an order-of-magnitude guidance ("a few thousand characters", "tens of submissions per window") while still deferring the exact figure to plan time.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK023 Are recovery requirements defined for a learner who crosses FR-013's review-flag threshold due to false-positive moderation calls rather than genuinely abusive content? [Gap, Recovery Flow] -- Fixed: FR-013 now explicitly states false-positive handling is out of scope until Milestone 7, same as the flag's review itself.
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for what a learner can do immediately after a moderation rejection beyond "resubmit" -- e.g., is their original (rejected) text preserved for editing? [Gap, Alternate Flow] -- Fixed: new Edge Cases bullet states rejected text is not preserved; the learner composes a new submission.
- [x] CHK025 Are non-functional requirements for the Grading Agent's own baseline availability specified, distinct from the per-request timeout/retry behavior already covered by FR-010? [Gap, Non-Functional] -- Fixed: new Assumptions bullet states FR-010's fallback is the sole mitigation, no separate SLA/uptime target, consistent with this project's pre-M7 operational scope.
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements defined for observability of guardrail-rejection *rates* (e.g., a spike in moderation or rate-limit rejections), or does the spec only cover per-event logging (FR-007/FR-012)? [Gap, Non-Functional] -- Fixed: new Assumptions bullet explicitly scopes this milestone to per-event observability only, aggregate-rate alerting out of scope.

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK027 Is behavior specified for a rubric with only a single criterion (weight = 1.0), the extreme case of FR-005's "weighted criteria" requirement? [Edge Case, Gap] -- Fixed: FR-002 now explicitly states this is valid.
- [x] CHK028 Is behavior specified for a graduated score landing exactly at the locked correct/incorrect threshold? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-005] -- Fixed: FR-005 now explicitly states a score equal to the threshold counts as correct (>=, not >).
- [x] CHK029 Is rejection-reason precedence specified in spec.md itself for a submission that would independently trigger more than one guardrail (e.g., simultaneously over-length and containing flaggable content)? [Edge Case, Gap] -- Fixed: new FR-017 (same fix as CHK016).
- [x] CHK030 Is behavior specified for a subject/topic configuration where no topic has opted into `free_text` at all -- an explicitly valid state, or undefined? [Edge Case, Gap] -- Fixed: new Edge Cases bullet states this is explicitly valid and unremarkable.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK031 Is the dependency on Milestone 1's FR-011 flagging mechanism's continued existence and stability stated as an explicit dependency this feature relies on, or only implied by cross-reference? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions] -- Fixed: new Assumptions bullet states this explicitly.
- [x] CHK032 Is the assumption that a free-text answer is submitted "once per question" validated against whether the client can actually prevent a second submission attempt, or is this purely a backend-enforced assumption with no stated client-side expectation? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] -- Fixed: the existing Assumptions bullet now states enforcement is server-side-authoritative, client-side prevention is a UX nicety only.
- [x] CHK033 Is the Grading Agent's continued existence as a reachable service treated as a hard dependency of every free-text question, with the "grading unavailable" fallback (FR-010) documented as the sole mitigation? [Dependency, Spec §FR-010] -- Fixed: new Assumptions bullet states this explicitly.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK034 Is it unambiguous whether FR-016's rate limit counts free-text submissions only, or all question types combined? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016] -- Fixed: FR-016 now explicitly scopes the count to free-text submissions only.
- [x] CHK035 Is it unambiguous, from spec.md's own Key Entities definition, that FR-013's "Moderation Flags" count excludes too-long and rate-limited rejections? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013 vs §Key Entities] -- Fixed: FR-013 itself now states this exclusion directly, not only via the Key Entities cross-reference.
- [x] CHK036 Does the spec clarify whether two Grading Agent deployments could ever serve different Grading Logic Versions simultaneously during a rollout, or does it assume a single version is always live? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008 vs FR-009] -- Fixed: new Assumptions bullet states a deployment is assumed atomic from a caller's perspective; mid-rollout overlap is a deployment-platform concern, not addressed by this spec.

## Notes

- Focus areas: security guardrails, A2A/independent-deployability, and grading-correctness/mastery-integration -- all three, per reviewer's "all of the above, broadly" selection.
- Depth: Standard (PR-review-level pass).
- All 36 items resolved 2026-08-19. CHK008 and CHK018 were fixed first (real defects surfaced during drafting); the remaining 34 were fixed in one batch at the reviewer's explicit request ("fix all checklist items") -- each edited directly into `spec.md`, adding two new functional requirements (FR-017 guardrail precedence, FR-018 distinct per-state messaging), six new Edge Cases bullets, and five new Assumptions bullets. `tasks.md` T027 was also updated to cover the newly-named fifth state (grading-in-progress) so it doesn't immediately drift from the just-updated spec.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate, built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify` -- distinct from this custom checklist.
